rationale: C15 provides a concrete, material template for the child: both directives establish an ordered succession among named or titled officers, select the highest-listed officer who is neither absent nor disabled, and authorize that officer to perform the department head's duties. The child closely reproduces C15's distinctive sentence structure while adapting the office, triggering circumstances, personnel list, and termination provision. C03's title suggests the same type of succession directive but supplies no operative text for comparison. C23 also concerns temporary performance of another officer's duties, but uses materially different, single-designee machinery.

shared_material.child_excerpt: During the absence or sickness of the Postmaster General the officer whose name is highest on the following list and who is not absent or under disability to perform the duties of the office of Postmaster General shall perform the duties of that office
shared_material.parent_excerpt: In case of the absence, sickness, resignation, or death of both the Secretary of Agriculture and the Under Secretary of Agriculture, the officer whose name is highest on the following list and who is not absent or under disability to discharge the duties of the office of the Secretary of Agriculture shall perform the duties of that office
shared_material.explanation: This is distinctive, closely shared succession language, with the later directive substituting the Postmaster General and narrowing the triggering circumstances.

shared_material.child_excerpt: 1. Assistant Postmaster General Vincent C. Burke. 2. Assistant Postmaster General Paul Aiken. 3. Assistant Postmaster General Joseph J. Lawler. 4. Assistant Postmaster General Walter Myers.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: 1. The Assistant Secretary of Agriculture 2. The Administrator of the Rural Electrification Administration 3. The Governor of the Farm Credit Administration 4. The Administrator of the Farmers Home Administration
shared_material.explanation: Both implement succession through a four-entry priority list governed by the same highest-listed-available-officer rule.
